# Command Registry

Every Yantra command and subcommand is described as declarative data in `@yantra/protocol`: its
path, arguments, options, execution class, effect, danger, option relations, exit codes and
`--json` result. The CLI's commander tree is generated from that data. A `CommandInvocation`
contract with a parser (`parseInvocation`) and a shell-aware formatter (`formatInvocation`) lets
any other surface describe, validate and display a command the same way the CLI parses it.

The value is that nothing can drift from the CLI. A surface that reads the registry knows every
flag the CLI registers, its help text, its default, how its effective value resolves, whether it
needs confirmation, and how the command executes. A command rendered for copying either runs
correctly when pasted into bash, Windows PowerShell 5.1 or cmd, or the formatter says plainly why
cmd cannot carry it.

This is a maintainer and integrator feature. The terminal is unchanged: `--help`, parse errors and
exit codes are byte-identical to the CLI before the registry, and 315 characterization goldens pin
them. Package internals are in
[Architecture: `packages/protocol`](../architecture.md#packagesprotocol) and
[Architecture: Command registry and program construction](../architecture.md#command-registry-and-program-construction).

## What It Does

### Describes every command as data

The registry lives in `packages/protocol/src/commands/` and is published both from the package
root and as the browser-safe subpath `@yantra/protocol/commands`. `COMMAND_REGISTRY` holds all 59
command paths, 7 groups and 52 leaves, in root-help order, with each group followed by its
subcommands.

| File                       | Holds                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema.ts`                | Zod schemas for the registry, entries, options, arguments, input kinds, precedence steps, conditions, execution, danger, relations and JSON |
| `groups.ts`                | The six named option groups                                                                                                                 |
| `entries/*.ts`             | Entries by family: `agentic`, `workflow`, `settings`, `runs`, `template`, `daemon`, `doctor`, `browser`                                     |
| `entries/builders.ts`      | Authoring helpers (`leaf`, `group`, `option`, `argument`, `exit`, `jsonOption`, `debugOption`)                                              |
| `registry.ts`              | `COMMAND_REGISTRY`, `LeafCommandId`, `LEAF_COMMAND_IDS`, `findCommand`, `findLeaf`                                                          |
| `validate.ts`, `errors.ts` | `validateCommandRegistry` and `CommandRegistryError`                                                                                        |
| `execution.ts`             | `executionClassFor` and `conditionHolds`                                                                                                    |
| `flags.ts`, `expand.ts`    | Commander's flag grammar and group expansion (`expandOptions`)                                                                              |
| `invocation.ts`            | `CommandInvocation`, `parseInvocation`, `createInvocationId`, `isAbsoluteCwd`                                                               |
| `format.ts`                | `formatInvocation`, `defaultShellFor` and the per-shell quoting functions                                                                   |

A **group** entry (`config`, `secret`, `daemon`, `model`, `sites`, `template`, `browser`) has a
description and subcommands, and no execution class. A **leaf** entry is an executable command and
carries:

- `aliases`, for example `discover` on `do`;
- `arguments`, in order, each with `required`, `variadic`, an optional commander default and an
  input kind;
- `options`, in help order, each either an inline option or a `{ group }` reference that expands in
  place;
- `execution`, `effect`, `danger`, `relations`, `exit_codes` and `json`.

Every entry also records `registration`. A `subcommand` entry is created with `parent.command()`
and inherits the root's `showHelpAfterError`; an `added` entry is created detached and attached
with `addCommand`, and does not. The difference is visible: only `ask`, `research` and `do` print
help after a parse error.

Each option keeps the exact commander `flags` string and help description, so help text is the
CLI's own. Its other fields:

- `long`, `short`, `attribute`, `value` (`none`, `required` or `optional`), `variadic` and
  `negatable`, all derived from `flags` by the `option()` builder and re-checked by validation;
- `repeatable`, which makes the CLI attach its `collect` parser;
- `default`, the **commander** parse default that help prints as `(default: …)`, absent when there
  is none;
- `mandatory`, for an option registered as required;
- `input`, the form-metadata kind (see [Inputs and Outputs](#inputs-and-outputs));
- `precedence`, `applicability` and option-level `danger`, when they apply.

`validateCommandRegistry(input)` applies the Zod shape and then the cross-entry rules the shape
cannot express. It throws `CommandRegistryError` with `entryId` and a named `rule` on the first
violation. Among the rules:

- ids are unique and equal `path.join('.')`;
- every subcommand has a group parent, and no group is empty;
- `long`, `short` and `attribute` are unique within a command after group expansion;
- every derived field agrees with the `flags` string;
- defaults agree with the value kind, and enum defaults sit within the choices;
- conditions and relations name options or arguments the command has;
- an `adapter` class needs adapter details and an `exemption` class needs exemption details;
- `json.flag` is `--json` exactly when the command registers `--json`;
- `exit_codes` includes `0` and has no duplicates;
- aliases do not collide with sibling names or aliases.

The shipped registry passes every rule in `packages/protocol/tests/commands/registry.spec.ts`.
Validation runs in tests, not at import time.

### Gives every leaf an execution class

`execution` has a `default` class, an ordered `rules` list where the first matching condition wins,
and the adapter or exemption details that class needs. `executionClassFor(entry, facts)` evaluates
it; `parseInvocation` calls it for you.

| Class               | Meaning (from the schema description)              | Examples                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run`               | Detached worker, slot counted                      | `ask`, `research`, `do`, `run`, `resume`, `browser check`, `doctor --agent-smoke`                                                                                                                    |
| `read`              | Host, in-process                                   | `list`, `show`, `audit`, `report`, `usage`, `schedules`, `profile`, `config path\|list\|get\|validate`, `model list`, `sites list`, `template list\|show`, `daemon status`, `browser list`, `doctor` |
| `mutate`            | Short-lived worker under locks                     | `config set\|unset`, `model add\|rm\|default`, `sites add\|remove`, `template new\|lint\|save\|remove`, `lint`, `schedule`, `unschedule`, `confirm`, `browser use`                                   |
| `exclusive`         | Blocks run starts                                  | `browser install`, `browser update`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `in-process-secure` | The value never travels in argv                    | `secret set`, `secret list`, `secret rm`                                                                                                                                                             |
| `adapter`           | An app-side adapter replaces the generated surface | `config edit` (`config-edit-yaml`), `init` (`init-onboarding`), `open` (`open-result-view`), `daemon start\|stop` (`daemon-control`)                                                                 |
| `exemption`         | A reviewed decision keeps it terminal-only         | `config data-dir` (decision `D15`)                                                                                                                                                                   |

An adapter may also say which class it executes as: `init` and `daemon start|stop` execute as
`mutate`. `confirm` is a `mutate` command that also carries the `confirm-inbox` adapter, executing
as `mutate`. `config data-dir` is exempt because relocation moves the directory that holds
the host lock, queue and sockets.

Three commands change class with their input:

- `doctor` is `read`, and `run` when `--agent-smoke` is present;
- `prefs` is `read`, and `mutate` when the action is `set` or `approve` or when `--forget` is
  present;
- `browser update` is `exclusive`, and `read` when `--dry-run` is present.

`effect` is the command's maximum effect: `none` (read only), `local` (writes Yantra-owned state)
or `external` (can contact websites, providers or download servers). `danger` is `none` or
`confirm` with a reason, and options can carry their own `danger`.

### Spells shared flags once, as option groups

Six named groups replace the CLI's old hand-written registrars. A command references only the
groups it uses, and the expanded options keep the old registration order, so help order is
unchanged.

| Group               | Options                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent-model`       | `--provider`, `--model`, `--thinking`, `--auth-secret`                                    |
| `agent-budget`      | `--max-duration`, `--max-tokens`, `--tool-timeout`, `--tool-retries`, `--confirm-timeout` |
| `agent-turn`        | `--turn-timeout`                                                                          |
| `no-llm`            | `--no-llm`                                                                                |
| `screenshots`       | `--no-screenshots`                                                                        |
| `browser-selection` | `--browser`, `--browser-path`                                                             |

For example `do` references `agent-model`, `agent-budget`, `no-llm`, `screenshots`, `agent-turn`
and `browser-selection`, then its own options. `doctor` references only `agent-model` and
`no-llm`, so it has no budget flags.

### Records how each effective value resolves

`precedence` lists, in order, the sources an option's effective value comes from: `flag`, `env`
(the variable name, optionally with a value it must equal), `preference` (a key in
`profile.yaml`), `config` (a key in `config.yaml`) and `default` (the pinned effective default,
with an optional note). The commander `default` and the effective default are different things: the
first is what help shows, the second is the last precedence step.

| Option                  | Declared chain                                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--provider`            | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_PROVIDER` → preference `agent.provider` → `anthropic`                        |
| `--model`               | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_MODEL` → preference `agent.model` → `claude-haiku-4-5`                       |
| `--thinking`            | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_THINKING` → preference `agent.thinking` → unset (the provider's own default) |
| `--auth-secret`         | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_AUTH_SECRET` → unset (managed credentials)                                   |
| `--max-duration`        | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_MAX_DURATION` → preference `agent.max_duration` → `15m`                      |
| `--max-tokens`          | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS` → preference `agent.max_tokens` → `2000000`                      |
| `--tool-timeout`        | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT` → preference `agent.tool_timeout` → `3m`                       |
| `--tool-retries`        | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_TOOL_RETRIES` → preference `agent.tool_retries` → `3`                        |
| `--confirm-timeout`     | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` → preference `agent.confirm_timeout` → `3m`                 |
| `--turn-timeout`        | flag → `YANTRA_AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT` → preference `agent.turn_timeout` → `2m` (at least 10s)        |
| `--no-llm`              | flag → `LLM_PROVIDER` equal to `none`                                                             |
| `--no-screenshots`      | flag → preference `context.screenshots` → `false` (screenshots need an explicit stored grant)     |
| `--browser`             | flag → config `browser.source` → `auto`                                                           |
| `--browser-path`        | flag → config `browser.executable_path` → unset (discover a system browser)                       |
| `ask --detail`          | flag → preference `defaults.detail` → `standard`                                                  |
| `ask --length`          | flag → preference `defaults.length` → `medium`                                                    |
| `ask --search-provider` | flag → preference `defaults.search_provider` → `auto`                                             |

`research` reads no preference for `--detail`, `--length` or `--search-provider`; its registry
entry records its real chain.

`applicability` lists conditions under which an option has an effect. The model, budget, turn and
`--no-screenshots` options apply only in `llm` mode, `--pipeline-timeout` only in `deterministic`
mode, and `--detail` only when `--format` is `terminal`.

`relations` declare only what the CLI already enforces, each as `conflicts` with a note:

- `--browser-path` is rejected unless `--browser` is `system` or absent, on every command with the
  `browser-selection` group;
- `--template` conflicts with `--no-llm` on `ask` and `research`;
- `report --open` conflicts with `--json`;
- `browser update --dry-run` conflicts with `--yes`.

### Generates the CLI's commander tree

`buildProgram(options, handlers?)` in `apps/cli/src/program.ts` builds the root program and calls
`buildCommandTree` (`apps/cli/src/registry/build-command-tree.ts`), which attaches every top-level
family in registry order. For each leaf it reproduces the old hand-written registration: arguments
with their defaults, `new Option(flags, description)`, `.default()` only when a commander default is
declared, `.choices()` only for parser-enforced enums, the `collect` parser for repeatable options,
`makeOptionMandatory()`, aliases, `addHelpText('after', …)`, and the registration style.

Leaves are bound by id to the table from `buildHandlers()` (`apps/cli/src/registry/handlers.ts`).
Its `satisfies Record<LeafCommandId, HandlerBinding>` makes an unbound leaf a typecheck error, and
the generator throws `CommandRegistryError` with rule `missing-handler` if a generated leaf has no
function at startup. A handler is commander-shaped: `(args, options, command)`, where `args` holds
positional values in declaration order. `fromAction` adapts an existing commander action
(`(arg1, …, options, command)`) into a handler, and `handler()` adapts a handler that declares its
own options interface.

`UNMIGRATED_COMMANDS` (`apps/cli/src/registry/unmigrated.ts`) is empty: every family is generated.
The legacy path in `buildCommandTree` remains for a family that ever has to be built by hand again,
and needs a dated entry with a reason and `owner: 'FEAT-070'`.

Command factories that other code still composes, such as `makeListCommand`, are one-line wrappers
around `createRegisteredCommand(id, handlers)`, so they are generated too. `attachRegistered`
generates one entry under a given parent.

### Parses an invocation exactly as the CLI does

`parseInvocation(argv, { cwd, invocationId?, registry? })` takes the tokens after the program name
and returns a `Result`. It never throws.

On success (`isOk: true`) the value holds:

- `invocation`: a `CommandInvocation` with `invocation_id` (a ULID, generated by
  `createInvocationId()` unless you pass one), the canonical `path` with aliases resolved, the
  `argv` tokens after the path exactly as given, and `cwd`;
- `entry`: the leaf registry entry;
- `arguments`: values by argument name, with commander argument defaults applied;
- `options`: values by commander attribute, with commander defaults applied, as `opts()` returns
  them;
- `explicit`: the attributes the user actually set;
- `execution`: the resolved execution class.

It replicates commander 14's grammar for this registry: alias resolution; options before, between
or after positionals; `--opt value`, `--opt=value`, `-p value` and `-pvalue`; `--no-x` negation;
repeatable and variadic values; `--`; `-h`/`--help`, `help <command>` and `-V`/`--version`;
parser-enforced choices; mandatory options; and missing or excess arguments. A root-level `--`
before the path is kept at the front of `argv`, so the invocation re-parses identically.

On failure (`isOk: false`) the error has a `code`, commander's own `message`, the offending
`token_index` when one token is to blame, and a `suggestion` when a close option exists. The codes
are `unknown_command`, `group_requires_subcommand`, `unknown_option`, `missing_option_value`,
`missing_argument`, `too_many_arguments`, `invalid_choice`, `missing_required_option`,
`help_or_version` and `invalid_invocation` (a relative `cwd` or a malformed invocation id).

`cwd` must be absolute: a POSIX `/…`, a drive-letter `X:\…` or `X:/…`, or a UNC `\\…` path. The
check is syntactic and needs no `node:path`.

### Formats a copyable command for each shell

`formatInvocation(invocation, shell, { program?, registry? })` renders the program, the canonical
path and `argv` as one command line. It exists for display and copying; it never feeds execution.
`shell` is `posix`, `powershell` or `cmd`, and `defaultShellFor(platform)` returns `powershell` for
`win32` and `posix` otherwise. `program` defaults to `yantra` and may be one token or several, such
as `['node', '/abs path/bin.js']`.

| Shell        | Quoting                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `posix`      | Bare when the token matches `[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+`; otherwise single-quoted, with `'` written as `'\''`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `powershell` | Windows PowerShell 5.1 native-argument rules. Plain words and flag-like tokens stay bare. Any other token is encoded for the child's MSVCRT parse (`"` as `\"`, with backslashes doubled where needed), wrapped in literal double quotes, and written as a single-quoted literal with `'` as `''`. An empty value is `'""'`, and `--` is always quoted. A program name that is not a plain word runs through the call operator, `& '<path>'`. |
| `cmd`        | Double-quoted when the token holds whitespace or one of `& \| < > ( ) ^ , ; =`, with the same backslash rule. Refused when cmd cannot carry a token (below).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

The result is `{ ok: true, text }` or `{ ok: false, reason, detail }`, with two refusal reasons:

- **`shell_unrepresentable`** (cmd only): a token, including the program path, contains a line
  break, a double quote, a percent sign or a control character. The `detail` names the token and
  the reason, for example
  `cmd cannot run this command: argument 2 contains a percent sign, which cmd expands as a variable`.
- **`secret_input`** (every shell): the invocation gives a value to an argument or option whose
  input kind is `secret-input`. Today that is `secret set [value]`. When a command that takes a
  secret does not parse, the formatter refuses rather than guess where the value is. A secret is
  never rendered into a copyable command.

### Keeps the data honest with integrity tests

| Suite                                                      | What it asserts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/cli/tests/registry/cli-surface.spec.ts`              | Rebuilds every golden under `apps/cli/tests/fixtures/cli-surface/` from `buildProgram` and compares bytes: `--help` at widths 80 and 160 for the root, every group and leaf and `yantra help <top-level>`; stderr, error code and exit code for an unknown option, a missing argument and an excess argument per leaf, a group without a subcommand and an unknown command; and `version.txt`. Prints a unified diff of the first difference. |
| `apps/cli/tests/registry/tree-agreement.spec.ts`           | Every registry entry matches the live commander command at its path: kind, description, aliases, arguments, option flags in order, descriptions, defaults, parser choices, mandatory and repeatable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `apps/cli/tests/registry/completeness.spec.ts`             | Every live path has an entry and every entry a live path, in the same order; every leaf has an execution class and is bound to a function; `UNMIGRATED_COMMANDS` is empty.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `apps/cli/tests/registry/option-consumers.spec.ts`         | Every registered option has a consumer (below), outside the shrink-only `KNOWN_DEAD_OPTIONS` list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `apps/cli/tests/registry/precedence.spec.ts`               | Every option with an `env` or `preference` step resolves through its command's real resolver as declared: the environment alone, the preference alone and the declared default each give the declared result, the environment outranks the preference, and the flag overrides both. The `YANTRA_AGENT_*` and `LLM_PROVIDER` names the registry declares are exactly those the resolvers read.                                                 |
| `apps/cli/tests/registry/parse-parity.spec.ts`             | For every leaf, 200 fast-check runs of valid and near-valid argv: `parseInvocation` succeeds exactly when the generated commander tree accepts, and then yields the same arguments and options commander passed to the handler.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `packages/protocol/tests/commands/registry.spec.ts`        | The shipped registry validates, the class and data facts above hold, plus the danger guard and group-spelling rule (below).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `packages/protocol/tests/commands/format.spec.ts`          | Golden quoting tables per shell, each cmd refusal reason and the secret refusal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `packages/protocol/tests/commands/format.property.spec.ts` | For every leaf, 100 runs over an adversarial alphabet, all three shells and both program forms: formatting, tokenizing with a reference model of the shell (`shell-tokenizers.ts`) and re-parsing gives back the original parse, unless the formatter refused for a stated reason. Every leaf must round-trip at least once.                                                                                                                  |
| `packages/protocol/tests/commands/boundary.spec.ts`        | Nothing under `src/commands/` imports a Node built-in or anything outside `src/commands/` and `src/utils/`, and the built module graph of `dist/commands/index.js` has no `node:` specifier.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `e2e/command-format-shells.spec.ts`                        | Real-shell execution (below).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

**Option consumers.** The consumer analysis uses the TypeScript compiler API, not regular
expressions, over the leaf's handler module (`apps/cli/src/commands/<top-level name>.ts`) and the
modules it imports directly from `apps/cli/src`. An inline option is consumed when its attribute is
read (`options.x`, `opts.x`, `options['x']` or destructured). A group option is consumed when the
module calls the group's resolver and reads its marker:

- `agent-model`: `resolveAgentInvocation` (or `resolveAgent`) called and `.model` or `.auth` read;
- `agent-budget`: the resolver called and `.budgets` read;
- `agent-turn`: the resolver called and `.turnTimeoutMs` or `.budgets` read;
- `no-llm`: the agent resolver or `noLlmReason` called;
- `screenshots`: `.screenshots` read;
- `browser-selection`: `resolveBrowserSelectionOverride` called.

`KNOWN_DEAD_OPTIONS` holds the hand-verified exceptions, each dated `2026-11-03` with evidence and a
TODO reference:

- `run` and `resume`: the five `agent-budget` flags and `--no-screenshots` (kind `unread`);
- `run --template` (kind `refused`: the handler reads it only to refuse it, and the refusal text
  `templates are not yet supported on run` must still be present);
- `confirm --debug` (kind `unread`).

The list may only shrink. The suite fails when an option outside the list has no consumer, when a
listed `unread` option gains one, when a refused option's refusal text disappears, or when the list
names an option the registry does not register.

**Danger guard.** Every leaf whose last path token is `rm`, `remove`, `unset`, `unschedule` or
`stop`, and every `--force`, `--reset` or `--forget` option, must have `danger: confirm`. The
exception table is empty today, and any future exception needs a written reason.

**Group spelling.** A long flag that belongs to a group may appear only through the group reference,
never inline, and each group option is spelled identically (flags and description) on every command.
There are two written exceptions, each a different idea under the same word: `init --provider`
(the installation's default provider, from a closed set) and `model add --provider` (the provider of
the model being registered, mandatory).

**Real shells.** `e2e/command-format-shells.spec.ts` runs a corpus of one valid invocation per leaf
plus `show -- <value>` for values built to break quoting: double and single quotes, `$HOME`,
`$(…)`, a backtick, `50%`, `%PATH%`, `^`, `!`, a line break, the empty argument, a leading dash,
Unicode, `& | < >`, trailing backslashes, an escaped quote, a tab, `; , =`, `@` and brackets. It
writes launchers shaped like the npm/pnpm cmd-shim templates (`yantra`, `yantra.cmd`, `yantra.ps1`)
into a temp `bin/` and runs each formatted command in bash (Git Bash on Windows), Windows PowerShell
5.1 and cmd, as `yantra` through the launchers, as `node <absolute echo path>`, and, for PowerShell
and cmd, as `yantra.cmd` explicitly. The target, `e2e/fixtures/argv-echo/argv-echo.mjs`, writes the
argv it received as JSON to the file named by `ARGV_ECHO_OUT`, so no console code page can alter
the bytes. The echoed argv must equal the invocation's path and argv. A missing shell is skipped
with the reason in the test name, and a cmd case the formatter refuses asserts the refusal instead
of running.

## How to Use It

### Read the registry

Import from the browser-safe subpath. It loads no filesystem code.

```ts
import { COMMAND_REGISTRY, expandOptions, findLeaf } from '@yantra/protocol/commands';

const doEntry = findLeaf(['discover']); // aliases resolve: the `do` entry
const options = expandOptions(doEntry!, COMMAND_REGISTRY.option_groups);
// Each option carries flags, description, input kind, commander default,
// precedence, applicability and danger; `group` names the group it came from.
```

`findCommand(path)` returns a group or a leaf and `undefined` for an unknown path. `LEAF_COMMAND_IDS`
lists every leaf id in registry order.

### Parse a command line

```ts
import { parseInvocation } from '@yantra/protocol/commands';

const parsed = parseInvocation(['discover', 'find the price', '--no-llm', '--browser=system'], {
  cwd: '/home/me',
});
if (parsed.isOk) {
  parsed.value.invocation.path; // ['do']
  parsed.value.invocation.argv; // ['find the price', '--no-llm', '--browser=system']
  parsed.value.options.llm; // false
  parsed.value.explicit; // ['llm', 'browser']
  parsed.value.execution; // 'run'
} else {
  parsed.error.code; // for example 'unknown_option'
}
```

`parseInvocation(['prefs', 'set', 'defaults.detail', 'full'], { cwd: '/w' })` resolves to `mutate`;
`prefs get x` resolves to `read`. `parseInvocation(['list', '--limt', '3'], …)` fails with
`unknown_option`, the message `error: unknown option '--limt'`, `token_index: 1` and the suggestion
`--limit`.

### Format a copyable command

```ts
import { defaultShellFor, formatInvocation } from '@yantra/protocol/commands';

const result = formatInvocation(parsed.value.invocation, defaultShellFor(process.platform));
if (result.ok) copy(result.text);
else show(result.reason, result.detail);
```

For the invocation `ask "what's 50% of $40?"`:

| Shell        | Result                                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `posix`      | `yantra ask 'what'\''s 50% of $40?'`                                                                                                 |
| `powershell` | `yantra ask '"what''s 50% of $40?"'`                                                                                                 |
| `cmd`        | Refused: `shell_unrepresentable`, `cmd cannot run this command: argument 2 contains a percent sign, which cmd expands as a variable` |

`secret set tavily.api_key abc` is refused with `secret_input` in every shell; `secret set
tavily.api_key`, which takes the value from a prompt or piped input, formats normally.

### Add or change a command

1. Edit the entry in `packages/protocol/src/commands/entries/<family>.ts` with the builders
   (`leaf`, `option`, `argument`, `exit`). Reference groups for shared flags rather than spelling
   them inline. A new entry also goes into `ENTRIES` in `registry.ts` at its root-help position,
   right after its group if it is a subcommand.
2. Put the action body in an exported handler in `apps/cli/src/commands/<top-level name>.ts`, and
   bind it by leaf id in `buildHandlers()`. The typecheck fails until every leaf is bound.
3. Rebuild protocol before trusting any CLI result, because `apps/cli` resolves it from `dist/`:
   `npx turbo run build --filter=@yantra/protocol`.
4. Run the suites. Any change to help text, a default or the command list fails
   `cli-surface.spec.ts`, which is the point. If the change is intended, recapture the goldens on
   purpose from `apps/cli` with `npx tsx scripts/capture-cli-surface.ts --overwrite` and review the
   diff. Never run prettier over `apps/cli/tests/fixtures/cli-surface/`; the files are byte-compared
   and listed in `.prettierignore`.
5. If the new option reads a value from the environment or a preference, declare the chain in
   `precedence`; `precedence.spec.ts` requires a resolver adapter for it. If the command removes or
   stops something, or the option is `--force`, `--reset` or `--forget`, give it `danger: confirm`.

### Run the tests

```bash
cd packages/protocol && npx vitest run tests/commands
npx turbo run build --filter=@yantra/protocol
cd apps/cli && npx vitest run tests/registry
npx turbo run build
cd e2e && npx vitest run command-format-shells.spec.ts
```

Every suite is tagged `@no-llm` and needs no model provider.

## Inputs and Outputs

**Input kinds** tell a generated form how to collect a value: `text`, `bool`, `duration`,
`workflow-ref`, `template-ref`, `run-ref`, `secret-input`, `enum` (`choices` and `enforced_by`),
`number` (`integer`, optional `min`) and `path` (`target` `file` or `dir`). Only an enum with
`enforced_by: 'parser'` becomes commander `.choices()`, which changes help and parse errors; an enum
with `enforced_by: 'handler'`, such as the `prefs` action or `--browser`, is validated by the
command itself.

**Conditions**, used by execution rules and applicability, are one of `{ option, present: true }`,
`{ option, equals }`, `{ argument, in }` and `{ mode: 'llm' | 'deterministic' }`.

**Exit codes** are the subset of `0` to `4` a command can return, each with its meaning for that
command: 0 success, 1 validation, 2 execution, 3 environment, 4 user handoff.

**`json`** records `flag` (`--json` or `null`), `shape` (`document`, `ndjson`, `envelope` or `none`)
and `schema`, the exported protocol schema name. `ask` and `research` emit a `document` of `Brief`,
and `do --json` emits `ndjson` of `TaskEvent`. Most other commands have `schema: null`, meaning not
yet described.

**Emitted JSON Schemas.** The protocol build emits `command-registry.json` and
`command-invocation.json` under `packages/protocol/generated/json-schema/` with the other schemas.

## Configuration and Permissions

None. The registry, parser and formatter are pure and silent: they read no configuration file,
preference, environment variable or secret, and they write nothing. The precedence chains only
describe where the CLI's resolvers look. `@yantra/protocol/commands` imports no Node built-in, so a
browser bundle can load it.

## Limitations

- cmd cannot carry a line break, a double quote, a percent sign or a control character, so the
  formatter refuses those commands for cmd with `shell_unrepresentable`. bash and PowerShell carry
  every value in the corpus.
- If PowerShell runs the `.cmd` launcher explicitly (`yantra.cmd …`), Windows re-reads the line
  through cmd, which expands a `%NAME%` pair (such as `%PATH%`) and ends the command at a line
  break. No quoting survives that. PowerShell's own resolution of `yantra` picks the `.ps1`
  launcher, which carries everything. Because quoted PowerShell values are wrapped in literal double
  quotes, `& | < > ^` and a lone `%` do survive the `.cmd` route. The real-shell suite asserts that
  `%NAME%` and a line break still fail there, so a change is noticed.
- On Linux and macOS the real-shell suite runs only bash; PowerShell 5.1 and cmd run only on Windows.
- Some registered options are still dead controls: the five budget flags and `--no-screenshots` on
  `run` and `resume`, `run --template` (refused), and `confirm --debug`. They stay in `--help` to
  keep it byte-identical and are tracked on `KNOWN_DEAD_OPTIONS`.
- Exit code 130, returned by `doctor --agent-smoke` and by an aborted agentic run, is outside the
  0 to 4 range `exit_codes` can express, so the registry does not record it.
- `parseInvocation` mirrors commander 14's grammar for this registry; it is not a general commander
  parser. The parse-parity suite is what keeps the two in agreement.
- Most `json.schema` values are `null`, so a consumer cannot yet look up the result schema for those
  commands.
